title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Sales Development agent for autonomous lead outreach
summary: Hold: Microsoft has published Copilot Credit billing for the Sales Development agent's resources, contrary to the briefing's claim that no meter is published. Microsoft also documents how administrators stop agent instances and how their access is bounded; the briefing incorrectly presents these controls as undocumented.

claims.quote: Autonomous agent that researches, qualifies, engages with leads, scaling sales capacity 24/7.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not describe how the agent's data access is bounded.
claims.quote: The agent runs under a dedicated agentic identity (Microsoft Entra Agent ID) that exists as its own security principal in the tenant. Access is explicitly granted and policy-scoped so the agent operates only with assigned permissions.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not describe how the agent's reach is bounded' with 'Learn says access is explicitly granted and policy-scoped so the agent operates only with assigned permissions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/sales/sales-dev-agent/architecture. Narrow the matching open question to which permissions and resources your tenant will assign.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how an administrator stops a running agent instance.
claims.quote: You can block or unblock agent instances for the entire organization using the same controls available for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Blocking an instance stops it and any actions it's performing.
claims.fix: Replace the absence sentence and matching stop question with: 'Administrators can stop an instance in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > All Agents > agent > Details > Instances > instance > Block.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-agent-instances. Do not equate stopping new CRM outreach or cancelling a campaign with blocking the entire instance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; changes; Open questions
claims.claim: No price, credit rate or meter has been published for the Sales Development agent.
claims.quote:
All charges are billed consumptively via Copilot Credits:
The agent account, email address, and persistent access to Microsoft 365 resources (for example, Exchange and OneDrive workspaces) have a recurring charge of 100 Copilot Credits per agent per month.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket absence claim wherever repeated with: 'Microsoft publishes Copilot Credit billing for Sales Development agent resources: 100 Copilot Credits per agent per month for the account and persistent resource access, plus consumptive activity charges. The resource service description lists Frontier Public availability for December 1, 2026, with consumption billing beginning on availability; these terms apply to Public Preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-resources-for-agents. Keep GA-specific requirements open, not the existence of a preview meter.

claims.claim: All users can see the agent in the Agent Store.
claims.quote: All users can see the Sales Development agent in the Agent Store, but only users with explicit access can activate an instance.

claims.claim: The overview limitations table says only creator-agent one-to-one Teams chat is supported.
claims.quote: Supports only 1:1 chats between the agent's creator and the agent. Other people can't chat with the agent.

claims.claim: The multi-user article instead supports a group chat with one manager and up to nine supervisors plus the agent.
claims.quote: The Sales Development agent supports a Teams group chat with up to 10 people plus the agent. The 10-person limit includes one manager and up to nine supervisors.

claims.claim: The overview instructs customers who do not consent to potential cross-region or alternate-model processing to uninstall an installed agent.
claims.quote:
If you don't consent to potential processing of requests outside your selected geographic region or by different supported AI models:
Don't install the Sales Development agent.
If already installed, uninstall the Sales Development agent to revoke consent.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist's Supervisor-access review has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote:
Ask each instance's manager to list users with Supervisor access in their 1:1 chat with the agent.
Supervisor access is not a table row because Learn describes it as a chat command given to the agent by its manager.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence that treats a chat-command control as exempt from the table requirement, and remove the Supervisor-access checklist bullet if retaining the current table. The checklist review currently has no corresponding row; do not add a new row as part of this correction.
